problem: VLN has little data: R2R has about 14K training paths but over 200K possible paths. The standard remedy, Speaker-Follower's back-translated augmentation of randomly sampled paths, stops helping once about 60% of the augmented data is used, because random paths are arbitrary and mostly uninformative.
motivation: Humans cope with scarce navigation experience through counterfactual reasoning: they imagine what would have happened on paths they did not take. The authors argue the counterfactual paths used for augmentation should be chosen, not sampled at random, so that they are informative for the current navigator. A sampler of this kind can also let a robot pre-explore a new environment before it receives instructions.
key_idea: Train a model-agnostic adversarial path sampler (APS) with REINFORCE to maximize the navigator's loss on its sampled, speaker-annotated paths while the navigator minimizes that loss. The collected hard paths serve as augmentation data, and in unseen environments as instruction-free pre-exploration data.
insight: Hard examples chosen adversarially make better augmentation than random ones. On Seq2Seq, the SR-vs-augmentation-ratio curve for random augmentation plateaus at about 60%, while APS data keeps improving the model (+4.5 SR val-seen, +1.6 val-unseen). Table 3 shows APS paths are the hardest: Seq2Seq gets 17.7 SR on aug_aps vs 20.3 on aug_rand. They also cover the random paths: Seq2Seq_aps scores 27.3 on aug_rand, above Seq2Seq_rand's own 26.4. Pre-exploration has a sweet spot (15 steps for Seq2Seq, 40 for Speaker-Follower) because APS paths in unseen scenes are not shortest paths. It helps more in environments whose visual features differ more from training. Updating APS during pre-exploration degenerates into cycles and back-and-forth paths, so APS is kept frozen there.
method: Adversarial Path Sampler (APS): LSTM recurrent action sampler. It attends over panoramic patch features (ResNet-152) using the previous hidden state, takes [v_t, a_{t-1}] as input, and scores navigable directions via a bilinear product with 128-d action embeddings. For visuomotor navigators (Seq2Seq) the single-view feature is used directly.

Speaker back-translation: a Speaker-Follower speaker, pre-trained on R2R and kept fixed, writes an instruction I for each APS-sampled path P. In seen environments sampled paths are first converted to shortest paths with the same start and end nodes, to match R2R's path distribution.

Min-max training: NAV is updated to minimize its student-forcing loss on (P, I). APS is updated with REINFORCE using that loss as reward, with a baseline b equal to the mean of all previous losses (min_NAV max_APS L_NAV). This makes APS model-agnostic, since it only needs the navigator's loss.

Augmentation schedule: all (P, I) pairs from the adversarial phase form aug_aps, matched to 17K paths like Speaker-Follower's aug_rand. NAV is trained 50K iterations on aug_aps, then fine-tuned 20K iterations on the original human instructions.

Environment-based pre-exploration: in each unseen environment the frozen APS samples paths (no shortest-path planner, no human instructions), the Speaker annotates them, and NAV is fine-tuned (lr 1e-5) for a limited number of steps. NAV then executes each instruction once with greedy decoding (no beam search).

setting.backbone: LSTM-based navigators trained from scratch on frozen ResNet-152 features + GloVe-initialized embeddings: Seq2Seq, Speaker-Follower, RCM; plus LSTM APS sampler and fixed Speaker-Follower speaker
setting.training_data: R2R train set plus 17K APS-sampled paths with Speaker-generated instructions (same size as Speaker-Follower's random augmentation). For pre-exploration: extra APS-sampled, speaker-annotated paths in each unseen environment.
setting.observation: panoramic RGB features (Speaker-Follower, RCM); single egocentric RGB view (Seq2Seq)
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoints (panoramic action space); low-level visuomotor turn/forward actions on the nav graph for Seq2Seq
setting.privileged: none for aug_aps models (the shortest-path planner is used only in training environments). Pre-exploration variants access unseen val/test environments before evaluation (no instructions, no GT paths).

numbers_note: The per-split limit of main method plus three variants excluded these pre-exploration rows. Speaker-Follower + aug_aps + pre-exploration: test NE 5.9 / OSR 46.4 / SR 37.6 / SPL 32.4; val-unseen 5.2 / 49.1 / 42.0 / 35.7. Seq2Seq + aug_aps + pre-exploration: test 6.7 / 29.4 / 23.2 / 20.8; val-unseen 6.6 / 37.8 / 27.0 / 24.6. Baseline rows (no aug, aug_rand) are the authors' own re-runs with greedy single-run decoding and are lower than some originally published numbers (e.g., RCM test SR 35.9). The augmentation-ratio curves (Fig. 1, 5) and pre-exploration-step curves (Fig. 7) are figures only.
results: APS augmentation beats random speaker augmentation (aug_rand, the Speaker-Follower recipe) for all three navigators on every split. For RCM, SR rises to 47.7 val-unseen (vs 45.6) and 45.1 test (vs 44.5). For Speaker-Follower it reaches 38.8 val-unseen (vs 36.1) and 68.2 val-seen (vs 66.4). Environment-based pre-exploration adds further gains in unseen environments, especially SPL for Speaker-Follower (val-unseen SR 42.0 / SPL 35.7). The best test result is RCM + aug_aps + pre-exploration at SR 45.9 / SPL 40.9.
limitations: Gains over random augmentation are small for the strongest navigator (RCM test SR +0.6, SPL +0.1), and all backbones are older LSTM-era models evaluated only on R2R.

Pre-exploration needs access to the test environments before evaluation. Its APS paths are not shortest paths and can hurt with too many steps, so the step count must be tuned per model (15 vs 40). APS cannot be updated there without degenerating into cycles.
Data quality depends on the fixed Speaker's instructions, and in seen environments sampled paths must be converted to shortest paths with a planner.
